text.text: I lost my car keys in the hotel room at check out. I tired to call but they just put you on hold long enough to make it seem accidental! I just want to know if anyone turned in my keys. ?I mean simple yes no is fine. But just 150% rude that a prior guest calls about possibly someone turning in a set of keys with a big Jeep keychain on it I mean, I think if I could've asked the question instead of getting hung up on six times and waiting 30 minutes on hold in between I might've gotten my answers. I hate when people just disregard you like you're not as important as someone else to the woman who hung up on me three times after holding 15 minutes each time and then the other woman that did it three times to me also thank you both even when I was there, the front desk people were ignorant go to get complementary coffee in their eyeball and you're like you're stealing ! Typical. I would put a picture up but the big JEEP chrome key chain be a dead give away. Won't be staying there again. This is no 5 star hotel , I would think they could at least humor me and look in their lost and found. Should I fly down and ask did anyone turn keys in ?? Nah. Just paid for new ones. Expensive but worth not having to deal with people who just want your money . And don't care about your stuff or your stay. The owner is so cool , they have their own parking spot complete with night club stands and a sign " do not park here " that's pathetic. Have some one come paint you a spot ! Cheap . Can't even answer customer calls just put you on hold and leave you for 20 min of music then "accidentally hang up"

The front desk is understaffed and cant answer the phone most of the time. We were also over charged and all this on my wife and I 1st anniversary. I have many pictures but I will only post a few for now. I am still Hoping Best Western will see this and make it right some how. Other wise I will stay in other hotels that are much better and much cheaper then this location.

text.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️

This hotel earns a three-star rating primarily due to its location. Outside of that, the overall service and experience were subpar. Unfortunately, this property appears to have become complacent because of its proximity to Universal Studios—a trend I’ve noticed with several surrounding hotels. Many of those nearby properties have since closed, while this one remains open largely because the location naturally draws guests.

That said, both the rooms and the level of service reflect complacency rather than guest-centric excellence. The housekeeping staff were very inconsiderate, frequently opening and slamming doors early in the morning. While the hotel has a unique and visually appealing octagon-style hallway design around the elevators, it unfortunately amplifies noise significantly. Sound travels easily, making it very difficult to get a good night’s sleep.

The breakfast buffet, which retails for $22, was extremely disappointing. The sausage was dried out, there were no eggs available, the coffee station was empty, and the tables were sticky. I’ve honestly received better breakfast service at a Motel 6.

Maintenance and upkeep were also lacking. Issues included a tub stopper that wouldn’t stay up and toilets that ran continuously throughout the night. Overall, the property felt worn and poorly maintained.

I was especially disappointed to have redeemed hard-earned Marriott Bonvoy points for this stay, given the quality of the experience. Marriott should strongly consider inspecting this hotel to ensure it meets brand standards.

text.text:
Stayed at the Four Points by Sheraton Orlando International Drive near Universal and overall it was a solid, convenient spot with a few highs and a few letdowns.

The biggest win was the service. Every staff member we interacted with was friendly, helpful, and genuinely welcoming. Check in was smooth, housekeeping was responsive, and the front desk team made the stay feel easy and stress free.

They’ve also added a new arcade, which was a fun surprise and a cool touch, especially if you’re traveling with kids or just want something casual to do at night. The heated pool is small but actually really nice and relaxing after long days at the parks. It’s clean, warm, and perfect for a quick dip. The room views are a huge plus too, we could see Fun Spot and EPIC Universe from our hotel. The self pay cafe is a great touch. You can always book Universal/EPIC/IOA things right in the lobby. Plus theme park shuttles offer a great, convenient way to get to and from the parks…

Now for the not so great stuff. The rooms are pretty small and feel cramped if you have a lot of luggage. The overall look of the hotel is dated and could definitely use a refresh. Biggest downside was the cleanliness details. The curtains in our room were noticeably dirty and stained, which kind of killed the vibe and made the space feel older than it is.

Bottom line, it’s a good budget friendly option close to Universal with awesome staff and some fun amenities, but don’t expect luxury or super modern rooms. Great for convenience and service, just manage expectations on the condition and size of the rooms.

text.text:
Aged, Musty, and Not Worth the Price

We stayed at Four Points by Sheraton Orlando International Drive expecting a comfortable stay based on the Marriott Bonvoy name, but the experience was extremely disappointing.

The room had a stagnant, moldy, almost cat-pee odor that appeared to be coming from the bathroom. With no airflow, sealed windows, and no balcony or lanai, the smell lingered and made the room feel damp and stuffy the entire stay.

The property is clearly aging. The carpet felt worn and old, the furniture looked dated, and the room had that humid, musty feel common in buildings that haven’t been properly updated. The bathroom showed signs of age as well, with lingering mildew odors and poor ventilation.

Soundproofing is minimal. You can hear hallway noise, doors slamming, and outside traffic from International Drive. The air conditioner was loud and cycled frequently, making it hard to sleep.

Other disappointments:

• Outdated interior and worn furnishings
• Damp, stale smell that never cleared
• No fresh air or ventilation options
• Thin walls and noticeable noise
• Bathroom ventilation issues
• Overall “tired” and neglected feel

Parking was $20 per day, which feels excessive given the large surface lot and available space. Hidden costs like this add to the frustration, especially when the room itself is already overpriced for what you get.

Pros:
• Convenient location near Universal Studios
• Easy access to International Drive dining and attractions

Cons:
• Strong unpleasant odor in the room
• Poor ventilation and sealed windows
• Aging property with worn interiors
• Noise and loud AC unit
• Extra daily parking fee
• Poor value for the price

We booked expecting a reliable Sheraton-level stay, but the property felt neglected and outdated. Between the smell, lack of airflow, and extra fees, it was not a comfortable experience — and we would not return.

hotel_name: Super 8 by Wyndham Orlando International Drive
address: 5900 American Way, Orlando, FL 32819, USA

text.text:
I used Choice Rewards points to book a complimentary night at this hotel, and the experience has been nothing short of shocking. The front desk staff checked me in on their system, but then refused to actually give me a room unless I paid a $150 deposit — even though other guests were being charged $100 or less. When I asked why my deposit was higher, I was given no explanation at all.

To make matters worse, they never cancelled my reservation in the Choice system. They marked me as “checked in” and told Choice I was already in the room, which is completely false. Because of this, Choice customer service believed I was accommodated, and I was left outside in the cold and rain with nowhere to go late at night.

I’ve been a Choice Diamond member for almost 3 years, and I have NEVER been treated like this. I called Choice multiple times for help, and I was hung up on repeatedly because the hotel was reporting that I was already checked into my room. Meanwhile, I was literally outside the property with my luggage, soaking wet and freezing.

The room is not double-booked, not unavailable, and not occupied whatsoever the front desk simply refused to honor my reward stay while still keeping me marked as checked in. This is extremely shady behavior and feels like the property is scamming Choice by claiming guests are in rooms that they never provided.
There was no compassion, no problem-solving, no attempt to help, and no honesty. Just refusal, runaround, and misrepresentation.

I have stayed at Choice properties across the country for years without issues, so I am genuinely stunned by the treatment I received here. I will not return to this location, and I strongly urge other Choice members to be cautious when booking this property.

text.text:
Took about 30 minutes to check in - only two clerks available with a line of about 20 to 25 people on a Saturday night (peak cruise passenger arrivals) including those on my bus coming in on the bus from the airport.

Room smelled like sewer gas - first thing you notice when you open the door and walk in.  Other reviewers have made the same comment.  It was persistent, and bad.

Breakfast not included.  It’s listed in the room amenities section but there is a little asterisk afterward saying it’s not included. Deceptive.  I overlooked the asterisk when I made the reservation and was unpleasantly surprised when I went down to eat.  I paid. The buffet in its entirety consisted of dry overcooked scrambled eggs, bad sausage, cold potatoes, an apple or orange, and white bread for toast.  Nothing else.  $27 for 2 people.

This place is overpriced for what it is.   I won’t stay here again.

text.text: This is a decent place to stay. No amenities or anything spectacular. Hotel restaurant is nothing to write home about but the service made up for EVERYTHING. The shuttle driver was so kind and hospitable. Yiraldi greeted us when we got there and helped us store our luggage and gave us a key card for the restroom until our room was ready. Upon leaving, I was trying to find a bottle of water and the machine wasn’t working and took my money and my Uber had arrived. When Yiraldi heard of this, she ran (literally) to the restaurant and got me a bottle of water. So kind, thoughtful and above and beyond service that I’ve never seen before!

text.text: Very disappointed in my recent experience. At no time was i warned that the hotel was not equipped with heat. I was given 2 extra blankets in a room with a temperature in the 50's. I spent the night sitting on the bathroom floor running the hair dryer for heat. I was not offered a refund on my points or the opportunity to switch to a hotel in the same network. I am still in shock that this hotel was even open during extreme cold with no heat. That is simple corporate greed. I would have gone camping if I had known I was going to sleep on the ground and freeze. Absolutely appalling-no apologies were given. Airport shuttle runs every 30 minutes.

text.text:
Online photos are misleading.
Starting with the airport shuttle, when I called and asked where to get picked up they told me anywhere between doors 1-15, we were at doors 12 and the bus WOULD NOT STOP. We were waving him down, there was another couple near us trying to catch the same shuttle and that man was sprinting trying to flag down the driver. He eventually stopped down at door 16 and only stopped for about 1 minute and started closing the doors as that man was still running towards him and yelling. Then we get to the hotel and as soon as we walk in we see the lobby is very run down and does not look like the photos online. We have to put down a $100 damage deposit which we didn’t know about. But we got it back do it wasn’t a big deal but not everyone would be prepared to do that. Then we got to the room which was not the room we reserved (different size bed) and it smelled weird. The door did not have the latch to lock it. Rust in the bathroom, shower tiles appeared dirty, could not get hot or even warm water in the shower (even tried waiting for a good amount of time). Breakfast is no longer included, and for people who drive themselves there, you have to pay to park in addition to what you paid to stay there.

text.text: I rarely leave negative reviews but this hotel was the definition of a complete disappointment, especially for the price. The rooms while updated are poorly maintained and very dirty, with stains on towels and robes. The reception staff doesn’t utilize common sense when issue arise such as returning calls with updates when the walls are vibrating due to the “air conditioning on the roof” resulting in the ability to sleep through the next. The bathroom sink didn’t not properly drain, the toilet doesn’t flush, balcony furniture is dirty and there is dirt/dust/grime throughout room. I’ve had better service and cleanliness at a Courtyard Marriott let alone an Autograph Collection.  The staff also failed to explain what was included in the resort fee or how to utilize. The beach “ran out of towels” and didn’t say that until being asked and after staying for multiple nights the “Daily Hand Fruit Bowl” was non existent as a platinum member so it’s unclear what I was paying for. When I ordered food/drink by the pool I was not provided what I ordered first time and when I tried to order room service many items weren’t available. On a positive note- they have great happy hour at the restaurant with very nice staff in restaurant/lobby bar. I spoke to management who expressed understanding of my issues but did the bare minimum to help having a pleasant stay. As a platinum elite member it’s unclear the value of the status if management doesn’t help make things right.

text.text: Arrived at hotel after booking a day room a few months previously. On arrival day room not ready, the receptionist looked realky awkward before explaining our day room advertised at 10am arrival was still not ready at 11am. WE are still sat here by the pool at 13.00 and day room still not ready. The hotel pool was full so we went up to the cabana pool, all beds taken and a cabana was free but $250charge. After juju listened to our woes she gave us the cabana free, that was lovely and a great service (I hope she gets promoted as what a lovely gesture, more than the hotel did). Food here was nice, club sandwich, and currently still waiting for our day room, but we have to leave at 18.00, let's see. Sahri our waitress was also lovely, can't do enough for us. So if you are booking a day room, be very weary of booking here, you can't guarantee getting a room but looks like hotel staff make up for lack of hotel booking system. If our room was ready I would have given 5 stars for service, again JuJu and sahri definitely bring the rating of this hotel up alot, receptionist could take a leaf out of their book. Eventually got the room atv4pm, so my suggestion is do not book this hotel for a day room 😕

text.text: Very disappointing. The lobby is nicely decorated and welcoming. The entire rest of the hotel is not in good condition. The corridor outside our room smelled of smoke; the room and the entire hotel smell very musty/mildew-y. The carpets need a thorough clean. The decor in the rooms is old and in some cases quite battered. There are marks on the walls and on the grouting in the bathroom. It just feel grubby and sticky and not sanitary. We found a large brown stain on the beach towel we were given on the pool deck. The pool deck itself needs some love too - peeling paint, stains on the walls. This is not a 4 star hotel. It’s not worthy of the Marriott Autograph designation. It should be closed down and renovated. On the plus side the manager canceled our reservation and refunded the room without incident.

text.text:
I wanted to be exited about this place but outside of the friendly guy working at the Starbucks in the lobby on 2/23/26 at 8pm this hotel is subpar to every other Hilton I have stayed at. Maybe the guy at Starbucks should be put in charge of the whole hotel. The $38 parking is an undisclosed scam.

We got to our room to find trash behind the TV. The remote control for the bedroom TV was missing. A big stain on our sheets and more. We called the front desk, concierge, etc. for 45 minutes with no answer. It took almost 10 minutes for the shower to get hot.

I can’t recommend this hotel. Stay at another Hilton property instead.

We also ordered food. As I said in another part of the review. Choose Uber Eats or DoorDash instead. 18% gratuity on everything. The food was average at best and they forgot half our order. Almost $100 for sandwiches fries and drinks is ridiculous.

Who has a pool and hot tub that closes at dark?  This hotel. When check in is at 4pm, You can use the pool and hot tub for 2.5 hrs. Zero value.

The rooms have multiple light switches that do nothing… so strange.

Still waiting on a tv remote. I’ll update if they finally bring it before I go to bed.

text.text:
Stayed here expecting a typical Hilton experience but was pretty disappointed.

First issue: the room never got cold, which is pretty frustrating in Miami. The AC barely worked and the room stayed warm the entire time.

Second: the pool situation makes no sense. The pool is apparently open to the public on Fridays, so when hotel guests try to use it, every chair is already taken. There were no towels available either, so guests basically can’t enjoy an amenity we’re paying for.

The closet handle in the room was broken, which just adds to the feeling that the property isn’t well maintained.

Service was also disappointing. The front desk staff seemed indifferent even with a long line of guests waiting, and communication was difficult since some staff members couldn’t speak English clearly.

Overall the hotel feels dated, poorly managed, and not up to the standard you expect from Hilton. The location near the airport is convenient, but the experience itself wasn’t worth it.

text.text:
Upon arrival at the hotel, we were told that no rooms were available yet, which was disappointing after traveling. Fortunately, the hotel is located near several markets, so we were able to pass the time while waiting. After about an hour, our room was finally ready.

Unfortunately, the experience did not improve. A repairman had to come to our room twice to address an issue with the air conditioning. During the first visit, he explained that the unit was frozen and said the thermostat should regulate within an hour. However, even after four hours, the room temperature remained at 75 degrees, which in Miami feels very warm and uncomfortable.

I later spoke with Linda at the front desk about the situation. Her attitude was very unhelpful, and when I asked if a fan was available, she acted as though it was a major inconvenience to assist.

My family and I have stayed at this hotel for nearly four years and typically remain for about three days after our cruise. Unfortunately, based on this experience, this will be our final stay. If our visit had been any longer, I would have preferred to spend it in the lobby rather than in that room.

First time staying here. It's an interesting location bc it's almost like an island. There isn't much around the airport itself, but there's a small plaza with some other food options. Otherwise you'll have to Uber or drive.

I liked the very convenient free airport shuttle. Pick up every 30 minutes or so. The hotel was spacious, nice staff, good food. Unfortunately it was a bit cold to hang out outside, but the amenities looked nice. Room was large and had a nice view. The hotel is a bit older, so some spots in the room looked well worn. Could likely benefit from some touch ups. Gym was well equipped and was bright and clean.

text.text:
First off, the staff here is absolutely wonderful. Many  are bilingual, (hey its Miami) which makes things very easy for people who do not speak English as their first language. We did not have a single negative counter with any hotel employee during our stay. Quite the opposite. They were very helpful.

Onto the rooms. Many people have given the hotel a lower rating because they say the rooms are dated. At hotels that get this much use, you are going to have couches that get worn out, etc. etc., but I think people are mainly talking about the carpet. The carpet is very clean and does not smell at all, but it looks like it was probably installed in the late 90s early 2000s. The dark green in the downstairs made me feel like I was in an old movie, but it’s all super clean.  I will include some pictures for reference. Like I said though, everything is super clean and nothing smells so… Does it really matter? The furniture in the rooms is nice-  very clean not stained. I like the artwork and the overall ambience inside as well. The views from the rooms are amazing. The hotel sits on like a little island in a lagoon so you have great views of the water on almost all sides. The only negative about the hotel rooms… Where is the microwave and the mini fridge? Our room had a mini fridge in it, but we were told that we could not leave personal belongings in it and we would have to pay a fee to have one brought to our room???That’s pretty ridiculous. Even the cheapest of hotel rooms have a microwave and a refrigerator so that you can store leftovers and then reheat them. I would highly suggest they bring those things back. I think that’s probably also affecting their room score.

The amenities are top-notch. This is seriously one of the nicest hotel gyms you might have ever seen. I was actually able to get my full workout in. The only thing they don’t have is a bench press, and I completely understand why for insurance reasons. Maybe they could add a Smith machine in the future to help accommodate that, but the cardio machines are great and they have many of them. There’s a full barbell section, and they even have a leg press! Like I said, one of the best hotel gyms I have ever seen. I was actually able to complete my workout, which is so rare when I’m traveling. The pool outside is beautiful and they also have a kids pool and a hot tub. There is a little walkway that goes out into the lagoon where you can see some of the wildlife and look out over the water and it’s really lovely. The only drawback to the scenery is that the airport is right across the water, but you know what that’s the price you pay for convenience. The hotel shuttle runs like a clock until midnight or so. We had no issues catching ours. I will say go to level G, not level two like it says on the hotel website. There’s a long row of hotel shuttle pick ups, (like 22 of them) and you can stand at one of them and pick up the Hilton shuttle from there.

Walk ability can be a problem here. There is a grocery store .8 miles away, and I walked to and from that with no problem. Just make sure that you use the proper pedestrian crosswalks. Do not jaywalk here. That could have disastrous consequences. Most of the places that you’re gonna wanna eat at and stuff though, you’re gonna need a Lyft or an Uber. The taxis here are super expensive so I would highly recommend using ride share service.

Walk ability can be a problem here. There is a grocery store .8 miles away, and I walked to and from that with no problem. Just make sure that you use the proper pedestrian crosswalks. Do not jaywalk here. That could have disastrous consequences. Most of the places that you’re gonna wanna eat at and stuff though, you’re gonna need a Lyft or an Uber. The taxis here are super expensive so I would highly recommend using ride share service.

All in all it was a very nice overnight stay.

I’m begging you, do not stay at this hotel. Thankfully, we were only here for one night, otherwise we would have left. Check-in was easy, however, the online check-in didn’t work. Don’t even bother doing it, just wait until you get to the hotel. Next, we called ahead of time to set-up transportation to the port. They said it was $14/pp and that we had to book at check-in. Okay; not bad. We went to book at check in and they told us we had to wait until the day of the transfer. We then waited until the next morning at 7:00 am and went down to book it. Somehow it was full, but there was no one down there? Whatever, we took an uber.

The worst part comes from the hotel room itself. The rooms are DISGUSTING. We found hair everywhere in the sheets, and it wasn’t our own. The bathroom is tiny. You can’t even open the door all the way as it hits the sink. You can barely turn around in the bathroom. The room had an awful smell. When we went to plug our phone charger into the outlet, the outlet fell completely out of the wall. The lamps were sticky and gross. The overhead light didn’t even work. PLEASE DO NOT STAY HERE. SAVE YOUR SANITY.

text.text: If you can afford it, go somewhere else!!Although the staff were nice and the location was literally a 12 minute drive to the airport terminal. The property itself was more than dated and not clean at all. I had got stuck in Miami from a missed connection and thought the smartest thing to do would be to get a cheap hotel near the airport. Although it was beyond their control for my trip. The shuttle never came and I ended up spending half of my room right on a taxi. (It only comes once every hour) I walked into the room and it smelled severely of bleach. So I thought well although not ideal at least it’ll be clean. I was mistaken. It looked as if they never really did an actual clean and they had just been doing a “cover-up “ job. Meaning doing things like painting over things instead of repairing. There were cigarette burns on the curtains, there was mould and mildew all over the bathroom. There was a zip tie on the floor underneath my door as if they had tried to unlock it during the evening. The structure was so old that every time somebody walked by my bed would shake. Sticky substances on surfaces. The staff were fine and perhaps doing the best with what they are given. But this particular location definitely needs more than an upgrade. I don’t usually leave negative reviews but if I had of gotten a tip off, I would’ve booked somewhere else and spent the extra 50 bucks and got a hotel where the shuttle actually came and I wasn’t afraid to touch things in the bathroom. All that said I unfortunately didn’t get to use the pool area but I walked in there for three minutes and it actually looked fairly decent… sorry to say days Inn I don’t recommend this property at all.

text.text: This is my second visit within 2 months at this hotel establishment. During my first visit l must admit, I was very hesitant, nervous and even scared. Why? I read the reviews first and it was so many nasty and negative reviews about the room conditions and how bad the staff treated you. I was imagining the worse things ever such as a roach infested room , dingy or dirty linen and towels. However, on that first visit, everything that I’ve read was completely far from the truth! I initially was going to have a negative experience, but that got quickly turned around then for the better. I ride a mobility scooter, and that day that I came the weather was very cold in Miami and rainy. It’s when we recently had a very bad cold snap in every part of the United States felt it. I waited over an hour for the courtesy shuttle to pick me up along with the host of other people waiting to get on. I was in conversation back-and-forth with the general manager, Miss M at the time, and she assured me that she was gonna allow her Driver to know to pick me up first and to be looking for me. When he finally arrive, I was bum, rushed by all the people getting on that bus. They saw me there as well and when I asked the driver, what about me he said he could not get me that he will be back in an hour because the bus was too full. I practically cried I’m cold freezing cold. I’m in a mobility scooter and unfortunately at the time I did not have money to take a Uber or a Lyft I called back to management clearly upset, but she turned things around immediately by saying go take a taxi and let the taxi driver know that we will pay them as soon as they get here.  I was very happy. Although it was just me the room that I had was a double room humongous very large room very clean very neat. That was something else that was debunked in my mind. Not only was the manager nice but the staff as well, very friendly and extremely accommodating. I feared going to their shuttle complementary ride to the port of Miami, which saved me even more money, of course, but I thought that I was only going to the same type of shuttle and get left again because of people going and filling up fast with luggage and everything But instead, they actually sent a huge charter bus like one of those Tour buses with the big big space at the bottom of the bus to put everything in which fit my scooter perfectly. Fast forward I arrived yesterday yesterday March 1 I called the hotel to let them know that I am here and once again warned them I have my mobility scooter. Miss S the other general manager worked there at this time yesterday and she called me and stated that the company no longer pick up mobility scooters immediately felt frustrated, but she said instead take a taxi and we will pay for it when you get here. An instant smile grew on my face and I absolutely love this place and every time that I have to take a cruise out of Miami this is where I will stay. I learned a valuable lesson and that don’t always judge things based on other peoples opinions, but truly try and get your own experience to develop your own true opinion. My opinion is definitely changed as I prejudged it prior to me ever visiting. I recommend this hotel for a couple of reasons for anyone to come to to travel. First and foremost, friendly, and accommodate staff, Second large spacious and very clean rooms with a very comfortable bed, Finally, the courtesy transportation from the airport, as well as the courtesy, free transportation to the cruise port, saving us a lot of money.

text.text: Did a quick weekend getaway for a friend’s birthday. We picked this hotel because of the location of the beach which was the only good thing. When we first arrived the gentleman at the desk seemed friendly until he told me how there is a $25 a day fee for the hotel (which was fine) I said I didn’t know that he told me I didn’t read the fine print. Then after checking in our room we had no towels or toilet paper and the AC wasn’t working in the room. I also paid for 2 queen size beds and the beds in the room were full size and also the shower was in the middle of the room which was not shown on Expedia site for this hotel. I went back down to the front desk and Terry told me I get what I paid for and that all the hotels in the area were double in price. Not the best customer service. Then we asked for more towels and the towels they gave us were dirty. We had to go buy our own towels and toilet paper for our four night stay. So if you’re considering booking here bring your own towels and toilet paper. I will never book with Expedia again!

Worst Hotel Experience in Miami – Never Again
This was hands down the worst hotel stay I’ve ever had in Miami. Absolutely unacceptable from start to finish.
First, they charged a cleaning fee for four days, yet housekeeping showed up only once. What exactly was I paying for? Definitely not cleanliness or service.
Any time I asked for help, no service was provided. When I requested fresh towels, I was flat-out told they had none. How does a hotel not have towels?
Breakfast was a complete joke — just coffee and boiled eggs. That’s it. No options, no effort. I literally said “WTH?” out loud.
The front desk staff were rude and arrogant. When my key card stopped working (which happens all the time in hotels), instead of fixing it professionally, they said, “We can’t keep doing this,” as if it was somehow my fault. Zero customer service, zero accountability.
This place does not deserve to call itself a hotel. Poor service, hidden fees, rude staff, and no basic amenities.
Worst Miami stay experience ever.
I will never come back and strongly suggest others avoid this place too.

text.text:
We were initially very happy with our stay—the apartment was clean, well-furnished, and offered a stunning view. The check-in process was smooth, and the host communicated promptly and clearly. These were the highlights of our experience.

However, what ultimately ruined our trip and left us deeply disappointed was the building’s elevator situation, which was not disclosed by the host in any way prior to our booking. The elevators were barely functioning throughout our stay. We often had to wait 40–70 minutes just to catch one, and on several occasions, we had no choice but to take the stairs—even from the 34th floor.

The most alarming incident involved my 13-year-old son, who got trapped in an elevator on the 23rd floor along with four other people. There were no working emergency alarms and no phone signal. They remained stuck until the doors eventually opened on their own. My son was terrified and ran down the stairs in a panic.

My husband, who is elderly and has mobility limitations, was effectively stuck in the apartment for most of our stay because he simply could not use the stairs. This situation caused enormous stress, physical strain, and completely disrupted the plans we had for our trip.

To make things worse, we learned from others in the building that this elevator issue is long-standing and well known—yet the host never mentioned it in the listing or during our communications. We felt misled and uninformed about a major safety and accessibility concern. Even after reporting the issue early during our stay, no meaningful action or compensation was offered.

At checkout, we had to begin the process hours early, anticipating long elevator delays, and struggled to move our luggage and help my husband exit safely.

While the apartment itself has potential, the ongoing elevator crisis and lack of transparency from the host made this a deeply stressful and disappointing experience. I would strongly advise future guests to ask direct questions about the elevator functionality before booking, especially if traveling with elderly family members or young children.

My first time staying here was last night. We had an after 10:00 pm arrival time into Miami. We were going to stay in the lounge however, it was already closed for the evening.
We were exhausted and decided to stay here since, it is right there in the airport and we could get some sleep.

The room was clean, and everything was freshly made. Our room was at the very end of the hall, so it did take a while to get from the elevator.
If, you don't mind the cost, I would recommend staying here just for the convenience of being in the airport. We were extremely exhausted and it came in handy for us. You do have to go back through security once, you exit the hotel. I didn't have any type of negative experience here.

text.text:
This review is for anyone who is vacationing here with the intentions of driving - meaning you rented a car and plan to travel by driving yourself.

I do not recommend this place as a place to do so. In fact - if you are driving I don’t recommend staying in Miami period.

It’s incredibly not-driver-friendly. The parking spots here are incredibly limited and extremely hard to park into. Unless you are renting a truck or a high-clearance vehicle, you will struggle. The way the parking spaces are located you will have to jump the curb. No way around that.

We stayed in room 208. The toilet does not flush. There was an unlined rubbish bin that we used to fill up with water to manually flush the toilets. The shower had little pressure. Anyone with long or lots of hair will find themselves showering for a long time.

If you are on foot however and you don’t mind the subpar room amenities - I actually think this place isn’t that bad. Just remember you will need to depend on either ride shares or the public transportation to get to anywhere.

I do wish that the property management company invest in upgrading their room card readers. The cards they use are extremely out of date and are extremely sensitive to data corruption. The receptionist who checked us in kept repeating herself to emphasize that the card cannot be near smart phones or wallet. Anything NFC or RFID capable will corrupt the card and you will be locked out of your room. Happened to us and other residents.

They do however have 24/7 front desk service so I guess it’s not that bad.

text.text:
I accidentally booked two weeks later than intended and immediately called the third party agent to ask for the 7 nights booking to be cancelled and I would rebook the correct dates (the online reservation calendar jumps to a date 2 weeks forward and highlights that day which misleads a distracted mind). They contacted the hotel who refused the request and would not transfer or allow a refund of any amount for cancellation. I decided to book another night and headed to the hotel to check in and try to negotiate a fair outcome. The receptionist reiterated the hotel policy which of course is not fair or necessary just because you have written acquisitive terms and greedy conditions into a policy.  So we stayed the night and turned out we would have abandoned our reservation anyway given the disgusting state of the property. The room and furnishings were filthy and of very poor quality. The walls are paper thin and the property sits on a main road so you are disturbed by noise from inside and outside the building. The ceiling fan was misaligned and also making lots of noise so had to be turned off. We dressed in track suits to minimize contact with the bed sheets which smelled like body odor and triggered formication or possibly we were actually being bitten by bed bugs. The WIFI is so slow as to be unusable and the staff were combative when we requested it be remedied.
It really is a two star hotel at best and the 2.5 stars they had needs to be amended.

text.text:
Sleep Inn Miami Airport is a very practical option if your goal is simply to rest before or after a flight. This is not a luxury hotel and it is not meant to be a vacation destination, but it does exactly what it is supposed to do.

The biggest advantage is the free airport shuttle. It was reliable and quick, and the hotel is only a few minutes from the airport, which makes early flights or late arrivals much less stressful.

The price is very reasonable for what you get, especially considering the proximity to the airport.

The room itself had everything needed for a short stay. The bed was comfortable, the bathroom was clean, and having a desk, fridge, and microwave was very convenient.

Everything worked as expected, which is really what matters for a stopover.

Check in and check out were efficient, but this is not a place where you should expect extra amenities or personalized attention.

Overall, this hotel is a great choice for one or two nights when you need a clean, functional place close to the airport with dependable transportation. It delivers good value and convenience without unnecessary extras.

text.text:
We have a back-to-back reservation as part of our stay was with a group. At check-in, I confirmed twice that we were checked in for the entire stay, specifically verifying the dates. Despite this, on day two, our keys stopped working, we were checked out automatically, and I even received a receipt by email.
After getting that sorted at the desk, we returned to our room at 3 PM to find it hadn't been cleaned. We called housekeeping to ask for service and at least some toilet paper (the room was out). When I called 20 minutes later to ask for an estimated time, I was given a rude "lecture" that I had only called "29 minutes and 29 seconds ago" and that with 350 rooms, they would get to us when they get to us. It took a second trip to the front desk to finally get this addressed.
Additionally, the bed was fitted with a sheet that was way too small, which immediately came undone. I asked the staff to change it and was assured it would be handled, but I returned to find the same sheet still on the bed. At this point I gave up…
On the bright side, Tyrell at the front desk was very helpful, and the restaurant service was excellent. However, we have come to expect much more from Marriott.

text.text: Immaculate, friendly, luxury, airport Marriott hotel!  Located minutes from West Palm Beach International Airport. This is a large, mature, traditional, high-rise hotel, providing all the amenities of a full service Marriott Hotel.  I enjoyed lunch at the restaurant, located adjacent the the lobby/registration area. The service was fantastic and friendly. The dining room and bar area Immaculate.  I highly recommend the "Marriott Burger ", it's one of my favorite burgers.  Whenever I stay at a traditional Marriott Hotel,  I always treat myself to a Marriott Burger!!  The hotel includes a beautiful,  tropical pool area and a market place store, providing snacks and beverages for purchase.  My guestroom was large and comfortable. Very quiet!  My guestroom had large windows providing a nice view of the water (bay). If you're traveling without a vehicle,  the hotel's restaurant is your best bet for dining. There are several restaurants within walking distance,  but the walk requires traveling along side busy roads. My colleagues and I enjoyed pleasant experience.  I highly recommend the West Palm Beach Marriott!

text.text:
I visited this place over New Year's Eve and I was not initially impressed. At check on they told us right away that the restaurant on site was closed for New Year's Eve and New Year's Day and so the have is $50 breakfast vouchers for our stay. What they forgot to say anything about was that The Bistro was a separate restaurant and that it was open!
My family was also given a room on the concierge level with lounge access but they also were not servicing that lounge for the two days that I was there so no hot food was available in there. Plus they seemed to be confused about the special holiday hours hours that they posted on the door of the lounge, access was unreliable.
Our room was nice but very cold and the heater didn't work. I called the front desk and told them about the issue and also asked for extra blankets and was told that everybody else was asking for blankets so they didn't have any left. They also said if engineering was available, they would send them up.... Nobody came the first night and we were huddling for warmth all night.
The next day I went to the front desk to complain and told them about my discomfort and they apologized and sent engineering up right away to fix the heater and housekeeping up with extra blankets.
This is not the level of service that I expect out of Marriott and this is not the level of treatment that I've grown accustomed to as an Ambassador Elite member. Being warm and informed could have made this a 5 star experience and I have other options while staying in West Palm.

We had a fantastic weekend stay at Casa Marina and genuinely wished we could have stayed longer. From the moment we arrived, the team made us feel incredibly welcome and well looked after.

Ronald at the front desk was an absolute star and went above and beyond to ensure everything about our stay was seamless. His attention to detail and willingness to help made a real impression and set the tone for the rest of the visit.

Christian and Lizbeth on the beach were wonderfully attentive and always nearby when we needed anything. Lea, our server at the beach restaurant, was warm, engaging, and made dinner feel easy and relaxed. Each morning Natalia in the coffee shop greeted us with such cheerful efficiency that it quickly became part of our daily routine. Cassie at the concierge desk provided excellent recommendations and thoughtful advice that helped us make the most of our time in Key West.

I also had the chance to meet Thom, the General Manager, who was incredibly affable and took the time to speak with us. He made us feel truly welcome, which says a great deal about the culture of the hotel.

I feel terrible that I cannot remember the name of our lobby bartender. He was from Moldova and was such a pleasure to chat with in the evenings. We also really enjoyed Gabe behind the bar, who was excellent. Our room was beautifully maintained, and every housekeeper we passed in the hall greeted us with a smile and a friendly hello.

The food was superb everywhere we dined, and the location made it easy to wander into town and explore Key West. I travelled with my girlfriend and her parents, and it proved to be the perfect setting for a relaxed family getaway.

We are already looking forward to returning. Thank you to the entire Casa Marina team for such a memorable escape!

Ronald at the front desk was an absolute star and went above and beyond to ensure everything about our stay was seamless. His attention to detail and willingness to help made a real impression and set the tone for the rest of the visit.

Christian and Lizbeth on the beach were wonderfully attentive and always nearby when we needed anything. Lea, our server at the beach restaurant, was warm, engaging, and made dinner feel easy and relaxed. Each morning Natalia in the coffee shop greeted us with such cheerful efficiency that it quickly became part of our daily routine. Cassie at the concierge desk provided excellent recommendations and thoughtful advice that helped us make the most of our time in Key West.

I also had the chance to meet Thom, the General Manager, who was incredibly affable and took the time to speak with us. He made us feel truly welcome, which says a great deal about the culture of the hotel.

I feel terrible that I cannot remember the name of our lobby bartender. He was from Moldova and was such a pleasure to chat with in the evenings. We also really enjoyed Gabe behind the bar, who was excellent. Our room was beautifully maintained, and every housekeeper we passed in the hall greeted us with a smile and a friendly hello.

The food was superb everywhere we dined, and the location made it easy to wander into town and explore Key West. I travelled with my girlfriend and her parents, and it proved to be the perfect setting for a relaxed family getaway.

We are already looking forward to returning. Thank you to the entire Casa Marina team for such a memorable escape!

text.text:
My parents and I just returned from a fantastic weekend at Casa Marina and it was such a special trip. The location is wonderful and made it easy to explore Key West, and we also loved spending time at the beach and around the property.

We had several great interactions with the team during our stay. Natalia in the coffee shop was cheerful and efficient each morning, and Cassie the concierge shared helpful suggestions that made getting around town very easy. Down on the beach, Christian and Lizbeth were attentive and always happy to assist. Lea at the beach restaurant was warm and lovely throughout our meals.

Ronald at the front desk truly stood out and made a real effort to ensure everything about our stay went smoothly. We also had two excellent bartenders during the trip, Gabe and another gentleman from Moldova in the lobby bar who was wonderful to chat with.

It was a relaxing and memorable weekend with my parents and we are already looking forward to coming back.

text.text:
If I'm honest, I don't understand the bad reviews about this hotel. We had almost perfect experience. Almost is because of the check in time, BUT the receptionists did everything they could, to make my experience better. Hotel was really full, the room wasn't available for early check in, which is fine, meanwhile we spend a bit time at the pool, but at 4pm, what is regular check in time, the room still wasn't ready. As apology i got a credit to spend in bars/restaurants there, which is great.
In general every single employee was really friendly, kind and helpful!
The hotel is amazing, the beach does have enough chairs and umbrellas for everyone. Also great, that they have two pools, one adults only and one family pool.
Valet parking guys are great and helping with luggage, opening car doors etc!
We had a breakfast at Flagler's, we ordered a la carte, but they also offering breakfast buffet. My kids did love they pancakes! And my avocado on sourdough bread was amazing! Also service was amazing!
We had a room in a suite wing, everything was perfect, really nice suite, clean and comfortable.
We'd definitely come back!

Regardless of third party or not it looks bad on Hilton and this is why i scored the “service” with a lower score.  Very disappointing with her help, we managed to figure things out on our own.

text.text:
The location of this hotel is great a lot of shops, stores, places to eat within walking distance and the beach is just a short drive.

The hotel offers parking, however, it’s coned off and you are responsible for moving the cones to get in and out of the parking lot. In addition, they demand that you to give them your car keys while you are at the hotel. They didn’t ask politely or even explain why they literally demand you hand over your car keys if you are present at the hotel. They have a man during the day that looks homeless who literally will chase you if you don’t turn in the car keys. This was very odd to me. On our 3rd night we needed more toilet paper. Upon asking the front desk for more comments we’re made that the people who give out the tissue leave at 4 and if you need toilet paper you should not have your “do not disturb” sign up. 0 hospitality. The rooms were very basic, beds were thin, pillows thin, had to keep playing around with the ac to make sure it stayed on. The room had a microwave and a mini fridge inside the same closet where you hang your clothes. So if you warm up food your clothes will smell like it. Not worth the price even with having a great location. I would never re-book or recommended this place.

text.text:
One might expect to have a peaceful and relaxing stay in a hotel, particularly in South Beach; however, my experience at the James Hotel in Miami, FL, was quite the opposite.

I arrived at approximately 3:30 PM on December 13, 2025, hoping to receive my room thirty minutes prior to the 4:00 PM check-in time (Confirmation # 9078866105381, initials J.A.).

The receptionist, who introduced herself as the "daughter of the hotel's owner," informed me she would impose a $10 fee for storing my bag, even for a few minutes, a $10 fee for "early" parking, and a $50 fee for early check-in. Interestingly, the lobby was empty, there was only one car in the parking lot, and it was only a few minutes before the check-in time of 4:00 PM. Furthermore, she mentioned a $50 per hour charge for late check-out. Her condescending and harsh demeanor was clearly intended to intimidate me, ultimately ruining my weekend.

While I understand hotels have their policies, this kind of rude behavior towards a paying guest is unacceptable and not a proper way to conduct business.

This individual's inappropriate behavior and condescending attitude are intolerable. Guests should not be treated in such a manner. It is particularly concerning as she claimed to be the "daughter of the owner" and threatened to cancel my reservation when I inquired about her name, which she refused to provide.

Although the room rate was relatively modest and the additional charges minimal, I see no reason to patronize this hotel.t is a fact that the hospitality industry is struggling and having a difficult time coping. I don't like writing negative reviews --- but, this is something that everybody should  know about.

Thank goodness AMEX Travel was able to cancel my booking and helped me through this ordeal.

Lastly, this James Hotel doesn't even look like it has clean & nice rooms since everything seems deary from the outside and at the lobby.

I decided to take the next flight back to NYC since I cannot possibly stay in South Beach with this unsettling experience in my mind.

text.text:
Air conditioning doesn't work and manager by far the rudest woman I've met.

Air conditioning didn't work in our initial room and asked for this to be looked at the next day. Reception staff were kind and helpful and said they would see to it. We got back later that evening and the room was exactly the same temperature. So went back to reception and again receptionist was helpful and provided us with an extra room (next to the original room).

Obviously the new room was extremely hot as it hadn't had the air conditioning running whatsoever so given the late hour I decided to move my belongings across to the new room and try to sleep as the room cooled. The new room didn't cool and I woke up drenched in sweat. My original room was still cooler than the new one so I went to try and sleep in there instead as it was now 4.00 in the morning.

The manager then woke me and my partner up SHOUTING that we leave the room. I explained the situation and the manager did not apologize for her tone or the condition of the room. She was totally out of order and even when she had calmed herself down did not apologize for her tone when talking to me or my partner.

We truly tired to be understanding about the condition of the room and I would not have left a negative review had the manager now been totally out of order. We cancelled our future booking for that hotel and I would urge you to do the same.

text.text:
I start this review while sitting in a Dennys at 1:40am, it being the only refuge with some comfort of home. In short, stay away. Just pay extra for a competent hotel, like Hyatt. Don’t be like us.

At 10pm on our second night we attempted to return to our room. The lock refused to open.

At this time we returned to the front desk, the receptionist was extremely willing to help with our issue. He printed new cards and told us they should work properly this time, as the hotel just went under renovation and the new system is finicky at the moment.

We return to our room and the new keys were dead on arrival. We quickly return to the front desk and tell him about our issue.

The front desk man profusely apologizes and follows us to inspect the door himself. After he inspects the door he leaves to find tools to reset the chip reader on the door.

Poor guy returns with fabric scissors and desperately attempts to fix the door in 50* temps. After a good 10min attempt, he calls in maintenance!

Unfortunately, maintenance never picks up. There’s no overnight maintenance at this cursed property.
The on call manager was UNWILLING to pay for a locksmith or nighttime emergency maintenance. Genuinely astonished at this nonsense alone.

We then get lead to another room to cover us for the night. This room has a rough working toilet, rust (I hope) stains on the floor, dust bunnies and a mirror covered in specks.

The time is now 3:05am, I’m exhausted and exceptionally frustrated with this stupid hotel. Safe to say my final night in Orlando will not be spent in this dumpster.

Never in my life would I think about my vacation being ruined with such swiftness.

If you skipped to the end. GO ELSEWHERE.

text.text: Do not stay here, we just had an incident of people breaking into my parents room and stealing their stuff, luckily the police department has a fast response. I am told by the police that this has not been the first time at this hotel. The rooms have roaches, rust everywhere, and seems like no working secruity cameras. Again DO NOT STAY HERE UNLESS YOU WANT THE RISK OF YOUR STUFF STOLEN WHILE ON VACATION. Aside from the breaking and entering the room is not well kept. The bathroom handle is not screwed on all the way, the hook for the towels fell out of the wall while somebody was in the shower and there is rust all over the dirty floors. We have been talking to other people who stay here and apparently there have been other incidents within the last week alone. A man and his wife were sleeping and somebody had walked in, we assume with a key card since their door was locked. Management is not here and they cant do anything until the morning. They have not been helpful in the situation involving the cops and there is no security. The hotel staff was completely hands off with this situation and they dont seem to want to remedy anything that has happened. There is blood on the sheets from the people who broke in and the hotel almost didnt accomodate us, we had to raise a little hell for anything to happen. Do not book here, its unsafe. We are lucky we are with a big enough group to be able to handle an incident like this. There is a lady a few doors down with her 2 kids and i am so glad this happened to us instead of her. Scary situation that you dont want to find yourself in. Update; they had a master key card to access the rooms. We found it in the room left on the bed.

text.text:
The hotel itself is great—friendly staff, a convenient location, and overall a pleasant stay. Unfortunately, the "complimentary one-hour bike rental" included in the resort fee felt misleading and poorly communicated.

When we checked in, we specifically asked the front desk about the bike rental benefit. We were told that the complimentary bikes were located just outside the lobby, and no additional instructions or requirements were mentioned.

The next morning, when we tried to use the bikes, we were required to enter a credit card. Since that wasn't mentioned before, we went back to the front desk and waited in line to ask about it. The staff member told us this was normal, explaining that the first hour was complimentary and charges would only apply if we exceeded that time limit.

Based on that information, we entered our credit card details. We were then charged $16 per person. We assumed this was a temporary hold or deposit that would be refunded after returning the bikes within the complimentary period.

At checkout, however, a different front desk employee informed us that we were supposed to enter a promotional code printed on a small card, in extremely tiny font. Because we hadn't used that code, we were charged the full rental fee. text.text:
We stayed in the Sorrento Tower, and while the view and location are nice, the actual experience was extremely disappointing for the price.

The room felt worn out and poorly maintained. Lighting was dim, the space did not feel properly cleaned, and the furniture on the deck was damaged, with broken and neglected items left outside. The overall condition of the room did not match what you would expect at this price point.

Basic amenities were a problem throughout the stay. The fridge in our room did not work, and food stored inside went warm. The bathtub would not drain, and the jets turned on randomly in the middle of the night, which was unsettling. The in-room washer and dryer were unusable due to a cut power cord, something we only discovered on the last night after loading it with laundry. Front desk staff had even sent detergent earlier, so there was no indication the machine didn’t work.

For a supposedly premium room, the coffee maker was the same basic Keurig you’d find in a low-end two-star hotel, which summed up the overall lack of attention to quality.

Check-in was also a mess. We were not given the correct rooms initially, and it took over half an hour to get things sorted out. On top of that, staff were consistently rude and difficult to get clear information from, which made the entire stay more frustrating than it needed to be.

Sorrento Tower is significantly overpriced for the condition and level of service provided. There are much better options in the area for less money. We would not stay in Sorrento Tower again and would not recommend it.

text.text:
Staying at Sorrento Tower in Fontainebleau Hotel, which I booked via Mak Property, was an absolute dream come true.
From the moment we stepped into our suite, we were greeted with breathtaking views of both Miami Beach and the downtown skyline – a sight that left us in awe every single day.
The sunsets from our suite were nothing short of magical, golden glow over the cityscape, creating an unforgettable backdrop for our evenings.
Speaking of the suite, it was impeccably designed and furnished with every comfort in mind. From the luxurious bedding to the spacious living area and fully-equipped, it truly felt like a home away from home.
The fact that it was serviced only added to the convenience and relaxation of our stay.

One of the highlights of our experience was the seamless access to all the amenities of the hotel and the beach. Whether we wanted to lounge by the pool, indulge in a spa treatment, or simply soak up the sun on the pristine sands of Miami Beach, everything was just steps away.
But perhaps what made our stay truly exceptional was the vibrant atmosphere that permeated every corner of the property. From the lively poolside scene to the buzzing energy of the beach club, there was never a dull moment during our stay.
Our stay at Sorrento Tower exceeded all expectations and left us with memories that will last a lifetime. We can't wait to return for another unforgettable experience in the heart of Miami Beach.

When we checked in, we were given a downgraded room. When we asked, we were told that the room we booked (edited: and fully pre paid for )was overbooked and given away. The first solution, we will give you two rooms for the two of you!  That made no sense. We ended up getting a room almost like what we booked, but not quite, and Im pretty sure it's a lower cost room. When we got to our new room, neither of the key cards worked, back down to reception.   Got in the room, and the pictures online are definitely staged, touched up pictures. Way more run down than I expected.
When you leave the front desk and head to the elevator, you are meet with a pungent odor of  musty mildew and stale air, and most of the hallways are the same, there is no air movement.

Now, for some other surprises. The pool is closed, as far as I could see, there is nowhere online thasts listed so if you looking for a hotel with a pool, nope!
Then the "breakfast"  they call it a continental breakfast, but bitter coffee and a muffin dies not constitute a continental breakfast. Even the front desk staff say, "If you want breakfast, go to IHop."  That's fine if we didn't pay for breakfast included.

It's definitely not worth the price we paid for the room.  I have to find a way to get some kind of refund.

text.text:
I booked this place via Expedia.com. Hubby and I were traveling to Miami from Atlanta on a late night flight. We arrived at the hotel a little after 1am. Definitely was not impressed upon arrival but we didn’t see anything alarming to catch our attention.

Check in was easy and quick. As we made it to our room we took notice of the dirty carpet leading to the rooms. Once we got inside the room - realized it was just mediocre. Definitely not how the reviews portrayed it (I am an “avid review reader”). The sofa/loveseat had very visible scratches in it (took pics & even called the front desk to let them know so they wouldn’t think we did it). Hard floors throughout so definitely make sure you have sandals so you’re not walking barefoot.

We were supposed to be in a queen size bed but it definitely looked and felt like a full size. The countertops in the kitchenette looked like they were newer but the room needs renovating/upgrading.

We didn’t see any washcloths so my hubby went to the front desk to get some. He came back and said, “they don’t have any”. So we had to wash with hand towels (I took a pic - definitely awkward & not appealing). There were cracks in the shower and it just needs to be upgraded. Shower head had rust.

Definitely not what I expected based off the reviews I read prior to booking. Did it do the job - YES! Would I necessarily recommend - NO! We just needed one night. It was close to the airport. Just my opinion - I wouldn’t pay the money to stay another night or come back.

text.text:
**WORTH READING***
This has been one of the worst hotel experiences I’ve ever had. When I arrived, the room looked dirty, and aside from the bed being made, it clearly wasn’t properly cleaned. On top of that, the night manager mistakenly charged my card over $400 for parking, despite the fact that I was already paying $370+ for the room. He claimed he immediately refunded the money, but when I checked out, I was told no refund had actually been processed until the GM handled it later.

I spent almost two weeks going back and forth with the staff. First, they refunded just $30, then told me they would only return $336 because of that initial refund—forcing me to send receipts, screenshots, and proof that they were consistently giving me wrong information. In the end, they still never refunded the full amount, and I had to go through my bank to get my money back, which took another 30 days.

Now, four months later, the hotel randomly charged my account $375 again—even though I’m nowhere near Miami and have not stayed there since. This is completely unacceptable. Not only do they make repeated billing errors, but they also offer no compensation, no apology, and no sense of responsibility for the stress and inconvenience they cause. They act as if simply issuing refunds—months later—is good enough.

This hotel should honestly be taken over by a company that knows how to run a property correctly and maintain proper billing practices. No one should have to deal with money being taken out of their account at random, especially during the holiday season.

text.text: Stayed 3 nights, joining my wife on her work trip to Fort Lauderdale. She'd stayed previously at the Delmar and had a great experience. Unfortunately, this stay was less than stellar. It seems the Element and the Delmar are sister properties, as they share many amenities and branding, communication, etc. The hotel is valet only, and they charge 5-star hotel valet prices. Our check-in process was slow and disorganized, and there was (I assume) a new employee at the front desk who was doing their new-hire training or some sort of training on the front desk computer, while a line of people waited to check in. The pool could be great, it's large and has plenty of seating (although the cabanas were closed and looked to not be used anymore) - but the seats are old and stained, the spot lights are damaged/broken and have duct or painters tape all over them, and the windows looked like they'd never been cleaned. The hot tub was covered with a wooden lid, as if it had been out of service for some time. The elevator situation is less than ideal: there's always a 5-minute wait, and on nights the rooftop bar is open, the waiting area is crowded, and it's clear they give preference to those going to the rooftop over their guests. The room was decent, but the shower was nice. The water pressure and the amenities provided were great. The in-hotel restaurant was closed for renovations, but looked complete, so not sure what was going on there. In each direction, the view directly next to the hotel is an empty plot of land ready for development - very bland with no vibe. Overall, 2/5 (and that's a stretch). Very disappointing.

text.text:
I stayed at the Element Fort Lauderdale Downtown and paid over $450 per night, which made this experience especially disappointing.

The elevators are absolutely terrible. It regularly took 5+ minutes just to get one. Because of this, I didn’t feel comfortable leaving my room to quickly grab breakfast or squeeze in a workout—it was that inconvenient. When I asked the front desk, they said all elevators were working, they’re just “very booked,” which doesn’t excuse the poor guest experience.

At check-in, I asked for water and was told there would be two bottles in my room. Instead, I found one empty glass bottle. By that point, I was exhausted and didn’t feel like dealing with the elevator chaos again just to fix it.

Breakfast the next morning was another disappointment. It was extremely crowded, and they had no plates, silverware, or cups available. When I asked, it took several minutes to get anything, and I was eventually given plastic silverware, which feels unacceptable for a hotel charging this much.

Overall, this was a very frustrating stay and not worth $450+ per night. Between the elevator issues, lack of basic amenities, and chaotic breakfast service, I would not recommend this hotel unless major improvements are made.

I'm writing this review as a warning to those who are considering renting a suite at the Residences via Airbnb and NOT through the hotel.  The Private Residences management company based in NYC that manages units in this building via Airbnb essentially STOLE $2,807.54 from me.  I'm shocked and alarmed at how little protection the paying customer has in the arrangement.   Airbnb is essentially indifferent to the theft.  And Fontainebleau management themselves has very little authority in the situation.

Had I known we had so little protection as a paying customer I never would have gone through Airbnb.

My wife and her girlfriends rented a two bedroom suite for 3 nights at the Residences via airbnb for a weekend getaway.  It was our first time using the service and it seemed like a good deal.  On Friday October 11th they checked into the room and found it to be dirty and in disrepair.  Attached are photos.  The deal-breaker issues were mold on the fridge and shower (one guest had allergies) and the poorly patched fist-sized holes in the walls (another guest was a survivor of domestic violence) There were also stains on the curtains, splatters on the walls around the toilet, scattered sticky spots, hair and clothing tags on the floor, etc.  Very grimy vibe.  They felt extremely uncomfortable and immediately notified airbnb and the front desk at the hotel.  The Host did offer another room to stay in, but they were exhausted & disheartened with the airbnb experience so they opted to cancel the room and purchase 2 new rooms directly from the Fontainebleau hotel.  And then things got sketchy.

The Host refused to check them out of the suite or let them cancel the reservation, and then went dark. The next day, the Host texted novels of excuses and accusations, how unreasonable they were being for not wanting to stay in the Suite.  The case was escalated within airbnb, but the Host was unresponsive.  Finally on Sunday my wife sat down with a manager at Fontainebleau owner services who was very kind, and she checked them out of the suite.  The manager said there was nothing else the Hotel could do,  but we did get a printout from housekeeping documenting that the room was never used.

When the trip ended on Monday, October 14th we followed up on the case with airbnb and were told that.......
1. You can't get a full refund because you never checked out of the room.
2. The Host doesn't have to check you out early if they don't want to, even if you ask them to do it.  The Host also doesn't have to answer you if they don't feel like it.
3. The maximum refund you can get is 10% for the cleaning fee and a $300 courtesy credit.
4. It's at the Host's discretion if you get a refund or not.  If the Host says no, Airbnb is powerless to do anything.  Airbnb takes no responsibility and won't cover your loses.
5.  Even though airbnb acknowledges the room was dirty and in disrepair, it wasn't dirty ENOUGH to qualify for any further action.

The first airbnb rep I spoke with issued an ultimatum, that if I didn't take the partial credit by the end of her shift she was logging out of her terminal and closing our case, and I would get nothing.

Finally after 3 weeks of back-and-forth with airbnb we were able to get a little under $1,000 back, but still lost over $1,800 for a suite no-one stayed in.  I've never had so much taken from me in exchange for nothing.   Please think twice before using airbnb (or any 3rd party site for that matter) when booking your vacation.  You have no protection as a consumer.  And if you don't like what you're being given they will just keep your money anyway.

text.text:
Vintage with a convenient location

We stayed at this hotel for two nights and appreciated its great location. It’s within walking distance of cafes and restaurants, making for a pleasant stroll. It’s also conveniently close to the train station (we took a train to Boca afterward) and just a short Uber ride from the airport.

The hotel itself is very vintage—old, but with a certain charm. However, it’s not for everyone. The rooms are small, and there is no elevator, so be prepared to carry your luggage up the stairs. That said, it seems well-maintained for what it is.

We didn’t have a car, so we can’t comment on parking.

Overall, we’d give it a solid 4 stars. Would we recommend staying here? If you're on a budget and need a location close to the airport and train station, this could be a good choice. Just keep in mind the vintage style and lack of an elevator.

text.text:
It’s cheap for a reason, which is okay, but they had horrible customer service.

I called prior to booking to ask about: shared bathrooms (whether it was referencing sharing with a roommate or sharing with other customers), the complaints about the AC units on their online reviews, the light exposure in the rooms, outside noises (there’s light construction near by), and if any of these are effected by which room I was staying in.

I spoke to someone who sounded like a younger man (I didn’t get his name), and he told me, in short, that my concerns were not warranted, and that it didn’t matter which room I booked.

As it turned out, it was not true.

They were willing to attempt to change my room to one with a private bathroom the next day, but the one night I stayed, the neon light completely lit up my room (as seen in my video at 2:30am), I had to share bathrooms with guests (despite expecting to have a private one), the incredibly loud AC unit ran inconsistently all night, and the construction nearby woke me up early in the morning (it was admittedly not horrifically loud though).

The hotel is fine for what it is, but I did not like being misled about what I was getting.

To make matters worse, the manager, Michael Omar Frazier, made accusatory remarks via email whenever I shared my grievances and asked (not demanded) if I could receive a partial refund for the remaining nights given I was misinformed about the hotel.

I was at a physicians conference and didn’t have the time to get into an email spat, so I attempted to call. Michael Omar Frazier was conveniently not around, despite me calling 3-4 times over the span of a few hours and him telling me that he would be in by 11am. I did happen to get the front desk to answer, and she said she would leave a message, but she first tried to tell me it was my fault for booking the wrong room, and that I just don’t understand how window units work. (And no, the manager never called back.)

Overall, just shameful place. It at least gave my colleagues a good laugh when I told them about my comedy-movie-bad experience.

text.text:
Arrived 9pm on a Saturday. Scheduled to stay until Monday. Went to my room, got ready for bed and was asleep by 11:30pm. Woke up at 4:30am to a cockroach crawling in my chest. I stripped the bed to see if there were more and I found bedbugs crawling along the perimeter seam of the mattress. I went downstairs to let management know but there was no one there. I called the number provided and no one answered. I called again and left a message a few minutes later asking for them to return my call. I put my belongings in a large plastic bag, tied it, and put it in the trunk of the car, parked in the sun, hope bf that would kill any bedbugs I left there with. Then I went to breakfast waiting for the call but I never received one.
I returned to the hotel at 8:30am and still no one there. I called one last time and no one answered. I left a second message at this time. I had work meeting beginning at 10am so I returned the keys and a handwritten message explaining the circumstances.
On my way to the meeting, I stopped at a store and purchased bedbug spray. I opened the plastic bag that was in the trunk and sprayed inside it until the can was empty. At the end of the day, I took all of my clothes and anything else that could be washed and took them to the laundromat. Washed everything in Hot water and prayed I wouldn’t take them home with me.
I called Hotel.com (I booked the reservation thru that site) and requested a refund. I sent the video of the cockroach and bedbugs. They reportedly reached out to the hotel and they were informed that they have strict cancellation processes and wouldn’t be refunding any portion except for $50 (paid $365 for the 2 nights).
It is suspect that Hotel Evernia spoke with Hotels.com because they couldn’t give me a name or copies of anything that was in writing. Possibly Hotel Evernia would have e refunded the money but then again, I left reviews, completed surveys, sent emails, etc and no one ever returned any correspondence. So maybe they did deny refunding the cost of the hotel.

I booked my room last minute so the price was a bit steep, but under normal circumstances this hotel is very affordable! the interiors are far from modern but it adds to the charm.

I booked a smoking room and was pleasantly surprised by the lack of musty scent. Rooms have a mini fridge & microwave, though no kettle, which is a shame.

There’s also a charming street cat that hangs out near the hotel. Staff were very friendly, although the front desk was sometimes empty.

It’s about a 40 minute walk to the beach here, but super close to the Brightline station, and not far from the Amtrak one either.

address: Key West, FL 33040, USA

text.text: We stayed Sun-Fri end of February 2026. We found the staff to be attentive to our needs, rooms comfortable and in good working order with regard to plumbing, fridge, TV, etc. Bedding was nice, we received extra blankets within 30 min of asking. Drinks and food a bit pricey, but certainly within expected range for Key West resorts. We rented a pool cabana for 1 day, it was wonderful. Stocked fridge with waters. Sodas, mineral water, and a large fruit plate as well. Towels and chaise covers readily available and personal attendants as well. While the resort is located quite a ways from the "main drag" of Duval St and Mallory Square as well as the main Marina, our group (late 50s to 70 in age) we still walked everywhere and did not need to hire other transportation. Only a 5 min walk to the south end of Duval which then extend 1.25 miles to the other end by Mallory Square. It was very chilly the first 2 days but when at the pool bar-restaurant area, the staff brought out space heaters which made it very comfortable. They also have beach blankets to snuggle under at the fire pits. If you're looking for white glove luxury, its not quite here, but this is a beautiful resort and we will certainly be returning here.
