Overall not satisfied with 5 star rating and the service and the room condition. We booked ocean view king room and they allocated a room which barely has any view in it and i had paid a grand for it. I asked front desk to give me another room and they provided me an upgrade of ocean view with balcony for $85/night. We have requested front desk to move our luggage from old room to new room (upgraded) and they left our selfie stick in the old room only. During checkout we told them that we are not able to find our selfie stick, they told us to create a lost item request and they will help us ship the item. When they found the item now they are asking me to pay for the label which is more than the value of item hence I would prefer discarding the item.

Rooms were pretty average and if you stay in 3 star hotel you'll get same room.

Overall, pathetic service. We requested to get our room clean and we were assured it will be done but when we came back our room was in same condition as we left it. Same experience in breakfast, I have requested an egg white omelet and I have been told that they can't do egg white as they don't have the material. I asked them if they have egg they can take the yellow yolk out and that will make it egg white. Common sense but the manager just came to me and informed they can't honour my request. Then I told them that you can't honour my request in a-la-carte but in your buffet live counter your chef is giving egg white omelet and at that moment the manager told me that they can honour my request. So they are not customer obsessed and not looking to solve the problem but just deny the request.

Overall the only good thing about this property is it's private beach and nothing else.

This is our second stay here.  We stayed the first time in the off season of September and I would say it was not bad and not exceptional 3.5-4 stars.  I read a lot of the reviews before coming here again for December 2025 and I must dispute a lot of what I read.  The staff was exceptional, they clearly outlined all of the fees upfront (resort, parking, etc.). This stay was exceptional.  I read about the slow elevators.  What are people expecting, Empire State Building express elevators, they were fine.  We texted daily with housekeeping and they would bring us whatever we needed when we had the do not disturb sign on our door.  The rooms didn’t smell, the a/c worked fine, and the entire staff was excellent.  It was a great getaway from the cold weather!  It’s not cheap but I would recommend this place to anyone.  We had a phenomenal time.  We’ll be back again.

And as a side note we brought our small chihuahua with us and most of the staff knew her name when we walked by.  Great time overall!

Overall, customer service/front desk employees were not hospitable, very uninviting and we kinda had to find our own way around Key West.

The rooms were basic for a “5 star hotel experience”. Coffee maker DID NOT WORK. We had to ask for more towels multiple times.
The balcony was beautiful though…

The resort was beautiful, but when you pay top dollar you expect top dollar service . What’s a beautiful resort with trashy service? Trashy.

Noteworthy: If this is a Personal Intimate, Non-Business vacation, you may want to pick another resort.

text.text:
Edit/Update: I don't know why, but after the owners read this review,  their lengthy, condescending reply filled with excuses was deleted.

Well, every other negative review has a response from the owner with a short, condescending novel with excuses thrown in offering no solutions or apologies, so let's see if the pattern continues!

The room was spacious and the bathroom was nice (Steel Horse Room). The bed was uncomfortable- blow up air mattress and the thermostat was automatically set to 75°, which was adjusted after expressing concern, so that was good.

We did not experience the "warm welcome" that the other guests had expressed. The owner let his dogs walk up to us, clearly overexcited, seemingly out of control, then he quickly yelled at them calling them Dumb and Dumber (not their names) and telling them to sit. This happened twice while we were there for 2 days which tells me this may have been done for attention. We ran into both owners a few times and were never asked how our stay is going. There clearly lacks a hospitality background/experience.

The food was extremely lack luster. I promise it won't exceed expectations. You'd get more quality and quantity at a hotel. The owners don't seem to have great social skills so when the older gentleman sat with us and another couple, the vibe was a little awkward since he's not friendly. The kitchen looks disheveled (not clean like a restaurant) and there is a hint of urine smell in the living room that we're 100% sure the owners are unaware of.

The house could use some basic clean up around the yard and the porch- this would go a long way for first impressions when walking up. The metal sculptures are mediocre at best which is why you haven't heard of this "artist" until you checked out the place online first. There are 2 old vehicles and a run down boat parked where the guests are supposed to park. I get the classic appeal, but make more room for the guests and remove that broken down boat. It's starting to look like a scrap yard.

Thanksgiving night we invited my dad over to chat in the living room and at 10:04pm the lady owner comes out and speaks to us like children that the quiet time is 10pm. I understand that rule, not far-fetched, but her communication skills were extremely condescending. It's a holiday night, let loose a little.

There are many aspects of this property that could be improved with minimal effort, but unfortunately the owners invested in a restaurant while admitting they've never worked in the industry 🙃 This seems to take away from the B&B.

We booked based on the warm welcoming reviews and 4-5 star place, but did not receive any welcome and saw a 2 star set-up. With all the flaws we would've enjoyed our stay, but they were not nice people. Theres no point in trying to express these concerns to the owners since they've been so distant and short with us. I can garentee this review wont be responded with solutions or apologies nor will the B&B be improved, refer to other reviews for reference excuses and responses. A little hospitality would've made all the difference. We're clearly not the only ones that had this experience.

text.text:
We had a very nice stay here but there were a few things worth noting that we did not like.
The hotel is currently undergoing renovations, starting with the penthouse floor and we were right below that so we heard quite a bit of the construction. The service elevator was clearly not working since the construction workers were using the guest elevators, of which there were only 2. This made for long wait times for the elevators.
Our room was ready for us immediately upon check in (earlier than normal check in time), which was amazing! And while it was spotlessly clean and had a stunning ocean view, there were noticeable holes in the curtains and shower curtain. There were many signs of wear/tear all over the hotel, making it clear why the renovation was needed.
The pool was NOT heated and this made a huge difference. Despite the 80 degree weather and warm (strong) winds, the water was too cold for me to go in and my kids even took a long time getting used to the water.
The beach staff were very nice and even came over to where the kids were digging in the sand to place an umbrella over them. There were also sand toys for them to play with.
The staff were exceptional. Front desk people were friendly, the cafe staff were amazing, and housekeeping did an amazing job keeping our room clean.
Would recommend this hotel for anyone on a budget.

text.text:
Extremely disappointing stay.

Check-in set the tone: the front desk didn’t greet me at all—when I walked up, the employee just said “ID.” No welcome, no smile. I also booked a standard room with one bed but was going to be put in a room with two small beds instead. I’m a Platinum Elite member and received no acknowledgment of status and no welcome gift.

The room itself was unacceptable. There was toilet paper with pubic hair on it in the toilet, hair on the towels, and what looked like blood or nail polish on the bathtub. The room phone’s service buttons didn’t work at all.  The key cards repeatedly failed—they had to be reprogrammed at check-in and then again the next day because they stopped working before checkout.  The view was of rooftop mechanical equipment that made constant noise day and night.

The property is also poorly maintained. Peeling paint, a peeling office chair in the room, and in the fitness room, the treadmill belt seam was separating, which is honestly a huge safety hazard.

Between the rude service, cleanliness issues, and maintenance problems, this stay fell far below what I expect from a Holiday Inn. Management should seriously address these issues.

text.text:
We stayed at The Lofts on Clematis in unit 405 and had a great experience overall. The room was very clean, and we did not experience any outside noise during our stay, which made it comfortable and relaxing.

We booked directly through the website, and management was very responsive through email. At first, I did not realize that all you have to do is reply to the confirmation email, and that is how they communicate. Once I understood that, everything was very smooth, and they always answered quickly.

Self check-in was very easy. They mentioned that instructions would be sent shortly before arrival, and we actually received ours about 20 minutes before the 4:00 PM check-in time. The keypad entry worked perfectly, and everything about accessing the building and room was simple and smooth.

Parking was also easy. About a block and a half away is the Banyan garage, where we parked from Friday through Sunday and only paid around $20 total, which was very reasonable.

On Saturday morning, the farmer’s market takes place right outside and brings a lot of activity to the area until about 1:30 PM, which adds to the lively atmosphere.

There is a vending machine on the fourth floor. It does not have a large selection, but there are still a few items available if needed.

Before staying, I had read some previous reviews on Airbnb mentioning occasional smells, but I did not notice any of that during our visit. The lobby, hallways, and our unit all smelled very pleasant. It’s possible there may have been city sewer work going on when others experienced that issue, because during our stay in early February we did not experience any odors at all.

The location is extremely central. We walked to several nearby hotels, and although they were technically walkable to Clematis as well, they felt farther away and had fewer things happening around them. The lofts are definitely in a better, more convenient spot compared to those.

For the price and the location, I would absolutely stay here again.

Good budget hotel but I have some suggestions that could make it better.

Firstly the rooms are a great size and very comfortable and the beds are extremely comfortable. Perfectly clean.

Our hallway smelt very damp and like feet and there was a dehumidifier running that was quite noisy.

Location close to the airport so it’s convenient.

But the main issue we had is the breakfast. There wasn’t a single plant based or vegan option available. No soy or oat milk to have with cereal or coffee. So much disposable plastic as well- not even a proper cup or mug to take a drink from. So not very environmentally conscious but I understand not wanting to wash up or deal with that afterwards. I think there could be a better selection for breakfast in terms of some vegetables or like not sugary cereals- maybe some muesli or granola. Coffee didn’t taste great either.

But otherwise the hotel is fine!

She knew how often I stayed with Choice properties and thanked me for my patronage.  I usually don't make reviews but felt compelled based upon her professionalism.  So although the property wasn't ideal, the professionalism of the HR manager and hotel manager was above reproach

text.text:
I booked this hotel as part of my 40th birthday celebration, a trip I had been excited about for months. My cousin and I planned everything carefully for our group, and we arrived in Miami two days early expecting a smooth, relaxing start. After seeing so many recommendations online, we trusted this hotel would be a good choice. It turned out to be one of the biggest disappointments of the entire trip.
We had three rooms, and every one of them had serious issues. My bathroom was completely uncleaned — not just missed, but genuinely filthy. I went to the front desk immediately, hoping someone would take it seriously, but no one ever came. I ended up putting plastic bags down just so we could shower. That’s how bad it was.
My parents’ room was even worse. They had cockroaches. I reported it, and again, nothing. No room change, no apology, no urgency. All three rooms had a strong, unpleasant smell, and we had to buy air fresheners just to make the stay bearable.
The washing machines didn’t work either. Traveling with a toddler, I had no choice but to walk to a nearby hotel to wash clothes. And I wasn’t the only one frustrated — several other guests told me they were dealing with the same problems. The staff acted like none of it mattered.
Breakfast was the same every day, and the staff would start putting things away before the posted end time. On our last morning, they began clearing the area several minutes early, even while guests were still trying to get food.
This stay added stress to what should have been a joyful celebration. I would never recommend this hotel to anyone.

text.text:
We booked a room at the Hotel Continental because of its proximity to the beach and its affordability compared to most of the Hilton properties south of 40th Street in Miami Beach.  We knew what we were in for in terms of amenities and room size, but were not at all disappointed.  The room was clean and the king mattress was great and we slept better here than in any Hampton Inn, HGI, etc which have huge welts in their mattresses.  Even the AC was smooth and calming.  It never woke us.

Leo checked us in and was very personable during our stay.  He had a great attitude about him.  Katy was very sweet and conversational with my wife and me.  She served us during happy hours and the next mornings at breakfast.  We loved talking with her and appreciated her hustle.

We used the hotel-provided, free beach chairs and towels each day and parked them close to the water’s edge, in front of the encampments from the neighboring Cadillac and Andaz hotels.  Our needs were simple this vacation, but the Hotel Continental managed to exceed our expectations.

I've stayed at many Marriott hotels over the years, and this was by far the worst experience I've ever had. We stayed from Thursday to Monday at a rate of $600 per night, which sets a certain expectation for quality and service unfortunately, this property did not meet those expectations at all.

In addition to the room rate, we were charged $75 per day for parking and a $35 daily destination fee, yet there were no meaningful amenities or services that justified those added costs. To make matters worse, one of our family vehicles was damaged while in the hotel's possession, which was extremely upsetting and added unnecessary stress to our stay.

The customer service was extremely disappointing. Staff were unhelpful and unresponsive, and there was no sense of hospitality or support throughout our visit.

The breakfast was another major letdown - $57 for food that was cold and of very poor quality. Overall, this hotel does not reflect a five-star experience in any way.

Very disappointing stay. We will not be returning.

text.text:
I am currently staying at this hotel and it is 1:30 a.m. as I write this review. I chose this property because it is advertised as a 5-star hotel, has an overall rating of 4.4, and is close to the cruise port.
When booking, I explained that we would have four people. The representative recommended a one-bedroom suite and assured me it would include two double beds, a pull-out couch, and a rollaway bed. However, the room we were given had only one king bed.
At check-in, we requested that the pull-out couch be set up and that a rollaway bed be brought to the room. We left for dinner expecting everything to be ready when we returned so we could rest after a long day of travel. When we came back, nothing had been done. We called the front desk and were told someone would be sent up. After waiting over 30 minutes, we ended up going to the front desk in person. Someone finally came up and set up the couch bed, but there was still no rollaway.
After both of our children showered, we were still missing the rollaway. My husband went back to the front desk and was then told that rollaway beds are not permitted in this room because of the carpet—completely contradicting everything we had been told previously. At that point, we were expected to have our 12-year-old daughter and 14-year-old son share a couch bed.
I went downstairs again, and thankfully, a very kind manager was able to get us a rollaway bed. I truly appreciate her effort and willingness to help when no one else would.
Additionally, the room was only stocked with two sets of towels for four people. It took a very long time—and multiple requests—before additional towels were delivered.
The room itself is disappointing. The carpet does not appear to have been vacuumed, and there is visible black mold around the edges of the shower, which is extremely unpleasant. At this point, I am still trying to figure out how I am going to sleep here. Both of my children are still awake, and even they feel like they are “roughing it.”
If you value a clean hotel room, I do not recommend staying here. If you expect timely service for simple requests like towels or bedding, I also do not recommend this hotel. This stay has been a huge disappointment, and it is not how we wanted to start our cruise, especially after such a long travel day.
I do want to acknowledge the very kind young woman at the front desk who ultimately helped us with the rollaway bed. She genuinely tried her best, and I am thankful for her assistance.
I have pictures of the black mold in the shower and even in the sink where you brush your teeth if I could figure out how to add it to this review from my phone, I will.

text.text:
I booked a Solo trip to Miami for 4 nights at this hotel. I thought the location was great, and from the pictures I decided to book the "Bayview penthouse". I wanted to relax with beautiful views, room service, and a cozy "penthouse". I use quotations because the pictures did not reflect the room at all. I was totally catfished. First off, the staff was very nice and helpful, so no complaints there.
But the room looked nothing like the pictures. How can a room go from being humid and hot to humid and freezing?! I had to request an extra blanket, because even 1 degree changes the temperature to unbearably hot to unbearably cold, and I'd rather have it cold. The constant humidity in the room made me feel dirty the entire stay. Speaking of dirty, thank god I brought my own hygiene products because there was no hand soap, and the bodywash was completely empty in the "if a toilet on any floor flushes the water pressure and temperature will drop tremendously" shower. There were also no bath cloths, and the shower head was corroded and uneven.  The penthouse(s) are on the 17th floor of the hotel, and with only 2 slow elevators and the constant cruisers, I ended up using the stairs way more than I wanted. Just to run down to grab my delivery food was an entire 30 minute ordeal. The wi-fi didn't reach that far up, so I had access to about 10 channels on cable, no wi-fi or streaming services even pretended to be provided. My last night the TV just stopped working completely. There is no "room service", everything online was a complete facade.
The restaurant/bar at the hotel was pretty good but pricey, and they were weirdly out of ingredients to make their specialty cocktails my entire stay.
Sure, I'd recommend this place for anyone staying 1 night, but keep your expectations very low. The ownership sucks money out of your pocket without providing even a quarter of the quality they pretend to provide online. Do not stay here. What a waste of money. I'm giving 1 star because the staff was very nice.

text.text: Classic bait and switch. Booked a room with a view and King bed. After checking and heading up to our room we walked into a  room with 2 doubles. I'm a pretty big guy that likes to sleep in the same bed as his wife which is why we picked a King bed. Headed back down to the front desk to see if they could resolve the issue and was told no Kings were available. Nevermind that we  reserved and paid extra for a King. When I mentioned about needing the extra room the guy behind the desk said 2 doubles are as much room as a king. After calling BS on that remark he said let me get my manager. The manager arrives and looks at our email reservation that states king, looks at his system and says it's our email that is wrong and not an error on his end and if we didn't want to stay in the room he would cancel the reservation. At this point is was about the fact they didn't take any accountability, never offered an apology or discount on the room that we paid extra for, just a "take it or leave it" attitude. No wonder they have a 3.5 star review which is about 3 stars higher then what they should have. Just try and make an effort to make your guests happy and reimburse them when mistakes are made. Would I recommend this hotel to a friend? Not a chance.

text.text:
I recently stayed at Cambria during my Universal trip and overall had a really good experience. The hotel feels very newly renovated, modern, and clean. For the price, it’s incredibly convenient and offers great value, especially if you’re visiting the parks and just need a comfortable place to rest. The staff were also consistently friendly and helpful, which made the stay even better.

There were just a couple of minor downsides. The hallway near the elevator on the 4th floor had a very strange and unpleasant smell. It was strong enough to notice each time passing through. I’m pretty sure management is aware of it because the hallway doors were kept closed the following day, likely to contain the odor. Hopefully that’s something they’re already working on resolving.

My biggest disappointment actually wasn’t related to the hotel itself. On the first night, our next-door neighbors were yelling and causing a lot of noise throughout the night until around 5 a.m. When I finally contacted the front desk, they responded immediately and handled the situation quickly and professionally. I honestly wish I had called sooner so I could have gotten more rest, but it was my first time experiencing something like that in a hotel.

That said, I don’t blame the hotel at all for that situation. The staff handled it exactly as they should have. If anything, it might suggest the walls aren’t the thickest, but again, the team responded right away when notified.

Overall, I would absolutely consider staying here again for future Universal trips. I’m not really a resort-style traveler, and this hotel checks all the boxes for a park-focused visit: clean, convenient, reasonably priced, and supported by a great staff.

text.text:
The hotel itself was pleasant, and the beds were super comfortable. My room was very clean, and the shower had good pressure with odor-free water. However, the shower area had no place to put my own products, and the hotel’s toiletries felt watered down.
The air conditioner didn’t work properly. Every time I returned to the room, the temperature had changed on its own, and there was an unpleasant damp smell that made the room feel humid.
Parking was too crowded, but there were nearby parking options available. Still, there was no proper sidewalk or safe pedestrian access to get back to the hotel, which made it inconvenient when carrying luggage unless you parked right in front of the entrance.
The front-desk staff were inconsistent. Some seemed irritated, as if guests were an inconvenience, but one gentleman during my stay was very attentive, and the woman who assisted me at check-out was genuinely kind.
I also found the atmosphere in the common areas uncomfortable, the hotel had a strong curry smell in the halls. For anyone who doesn’t enjoy that scent—or the food—it’s something to keep in mind.
Overall, the location was perfect but not with a quiet environment, the room itself was comfortable, but with all these other issues, I wouldn’t stay here again.

text.text: This is listed on Google as a 3 star hotel but it's somewhere between a 1 and 2 star hotel at best. Photos are misleading. Guy at the desk was nice and got me checked in. When I got to my room, I immediately noticed a pungent and unpleasant chemical cleaning smell that was almost starting to give me a headache. This is all in the midst of Storm Fern while I'm trying to get back home from a trip but stranded in Orlando indefinitely until flights get figured out and I already don't know if I'm getting comped for other additional expenses. So now I have to worry about $75 for a hotel room they I didn't use and would have had no way of knowing I would have needed to cancel until I walked into the actual room. Don't forget to look at the photo I included and ask yourself if it looks like it matches up with the photos they put online. Once again this is a 2 star hotel AT BEST.

text.text: After booking last minute due to a family emergency, my family including my sister, her husband, and their one-year-old baby  drove from Atlanta, GA and arrived around 2:20 in the morning. Despite the late arrival, everything went smoothly. The beds were extremely comfortable and the hotel was very clean, but the highlight of our stay was Marteen’s customer service.When I arrived, Marteen was assisting another group with an issue, and I immediately noticed how professional and responsive he was in handling their needs. When it was my turn, he quickly helped me check in. However, when we reached our room, we discovered it had one king bed instead of the two queens I originally booked.I immediately called the front desk, and Marteen handled the situation with great determination and professionalism. It seemed there may have been a system error and our original room was no longer available, but Marteen kept searching for a solution and stayed in constant communication while we waited in the room out of the cold.At one point, I stepped outside, and suddenly  heard footsteps running. When I turned around, it was Marteen personally bringing the key to our new room and apologizing for the inconvenience. His willingness to go above and beyond truly stood out. Marteen’s service was outstanding, and he represents the business exceptionally well. Professional, empathetic, and solution-oriented  all qualities of a great leader. I will admit this was not our first, second or third choice to stay here but because it was last minute we had no choice, now after experiencing 5 star customer service this is my 1st choice now! And where my family and  will be staying in Orlando moving forward!

text.text:
Very disappointing stay – absolutely not worth the price

This hotel looks much better in photos than in real life. The room was very small, and the entire property feels extremely old and outdated. Everything looks worn out — the furniture, the bathroom, and the overall condition of the hotel clearly show its age.

The bathroom was in poor shape, and there were almost no basic amenities. No toothbrushes, no toothpaste, no toiletries — just a single small bar of soap. For a hotel charging this much, that’s unacceptable.

The air conditioner was incredibly loud. It sounded like a tractor running all night, making it very difficult to sleep.

The only positives were the friendly staff and a decent breakfast.

We stayed just one night and paid $477 with taxes, plus a $25 daily amenity fee that supposedly included transportation to downtown Key West — which we didn’t use at all. Paying around $500 for one night for a place in this condition is simply too much.

Overall, this hotel is seriously overpriced and not worth the money.

text.text:
Our stay at this property was good. The pool was nice, free breakfast was fully featured, and the room was a decent size and clean. The pricing was also in line with not being close to the historic area of Key West, but is still conveniently located with a short drive to the historic area and near amenities like grocery stores. The service provided was good too.

With that being said, this is not the normal Marriott experience and a dated property. Some updates like comfy beds were made in the rooms already. When we left, they were in the process of renovating the rooms a few at a time. The renovations didn't disturb us at all, though it would have been nice to stay in an updated room already.

Given that the pricing is substantially cheaper than in the historic area, I'd recommend staying here if you're budget conscience and need a clean, family friendly place to stay. But know that it will not match what you expect from most Marriott hotels unless the renovations are complete.

In terms of accessibility, they had a pool lift chair. We weren't able to use it because the battery was not charged when we tried to use it. So would recommend reaching out ahead of time so they can get it charged up. Our room was wheelchair accessible with an elevator on the property to get us up and it worked fine with an accessible shower and easy to roll up to the sink. The bed was still normal hotel height and not lowered so that was inconvenient but workable for us.

text.text:
I think this was one of the worst hotels I've ever stayed at in the Orlando area. I've been to Orlando dozens of times, but since this was a Universal Epic trip, I decided to splurge on the endless summer hotel. For $150 a night, I expected better, but I was sorely disappointed. The room was not clean, there were hairs from prior guests, dust, and thin blankets, even though it dropped to 40F in February at night, they basically only provide a top sheet. The walls were super thin, we could hear our neighbors on either side and despite me asking them to please quiet down, neither cared even though it was already 1 AM and I was trying to sleep. The shower was sad, with water that did not get hot and only stayed warm, at best. Our showerhead did not work properly and despite us asking maintenance, they never fixed it. Our toilet leaked and did not flush properly, but when they did come to address it, the maintenance man was condescending and asked us to display the ability to flush a toilet.
The dining room is the equivalent of a hospital cafeteria, overpriced and poorly serviced. I ordered a grilled cheese, which was served cold despite the scorch marks on it from being burned. My friend ordered the fish and it was so dry, that not even sauce could save it. I do not think anyone should be staying at this hotel at this price point, unless being able to be close to the parks is a deal breaker for you, then maybe you can withstand it.

Just stayed here with my family. Great price on a 2 room suite. Hotel is clean, staff is friendly, and shuttle service to the parks is great though it took awhile a couple of times. I wouldn’t hesitate to stay here again. Only 4 minor negatives.
1. $26/night to self park.
2. You can hear so much through the walls. I could hear the neighbors alarm go off each morning. All night I could hear people walking above us. When someone knocked on the neighbors door, seemed like ours.
3. The bathroom door opens in with nearly no clearance by the toilet. My daughter busted her toe just trying to get out of the bathroom.
4. Someone vomited in the pool. Took them awhile to decide to clear it out. We only knew because another guest told us. They then called it unscheduled maintenance. We were told we could go across the street to the sister hotel Dockside. When we went over there, the front desk gave us a hard time about it.
But, even still, we enjoyed our stay. Front desk at Dockside was great checking us in. Gave my son a birthday button. Text us about an item we left at the desk. There are some food options within walking distance and a Walgreens across the street.

text.text: Surfside Inn & Suites was great for the price. Our only complaint was how much noise you can hear in the room. If the noise doesn't bother you, I recommend this hotel. It's the best price for having a suite. The hotel is clean and all of the staff is very friendly and helpful. We arrived at noon and our room was ready, plus they gave us a one hour later checkout. It is not within walking distance to the parks, but the bus is very convenient and we never had to wait long. It's only about 10 min to get to the universal/Islands of adventure parks and about 15 min to Epic Universe. We ordered room service pizza and it was very good and fresh when delivered. We had a one-bedroom suite which worked out great for us. I slept in the bed that was by the front door and could hear every noise in the hall way and room's surrounding us. I had ear plugs that I could put in to block it out so it wasn't a problem for me, but something to be aware of - sacrifice price for noise. Despite the noise, I would stay here again. I like the Surfside better than the Dockside because it is a little smaller, plus the bus between the hotel and City walk/Universal Orlando/Islands of Adventure stops at Surfside before Dockside.

text.text:
Just checked in for the next 2 nights and wanted to leave a practical note for other travellers—mainly so expectations match the product.

Positives so far: Front desk staff has been polite, calm, and responsive. When we raised the issue below, they gave a clear explanation without being dismissive.

text.text: Like 👍🏼 our review! We had a wonderful overnight stay at Albion South Beach Hotel in Miami Beach, Florida after flying into Fort Lauderdale to depart for our cruise the next day. We chose the place due to its solid reviews, walking distance to Lincoln Road shopping area and beaches, and great value for the price point. Overall, the hotel met our expectations and we really enjoyed the cozy bedroom with four pillows, clean bathroom with a tub, large closet and safe for valuables, reasonable internet speed for emails and searching, beautiful and comfortable lobby, quiet hallways for a good sleep, a small working gym, free morning coffee (after 7AM) on the mezzanine, and most importantly, a kind and personable staff. Please note that we didn't have access to the pool since it's currently being renovated during our stay and it was not a problem to us. Since we were on the third floor, it was very easy to take the stairs instead of the slow elevator. However, we enjoyed the access to a sleek bar downstairs for a late night drink and access to an a ala carte breakfast with a variety of offerings. Lastly, the hotel offered a luggage hold for the day allowing us to explore the area more before departing for the cruise. Given this, we would love to stay here again and would definitely recommend this place to our friends and family.

text.text:
We stayed here for four nights and wish we stayed elsewhere.

Pros
- Convenient beach access
- Rooms were stylish and we had good experiences with housekeeping

Cons
- Service was sub par for a five star hotel. The front desk and breakfast at the hotel at aguasal in particular. Upon checkin the front desk was ill informed of the pool/beach closure for the event and told us the beach was open to the public. Turns out only one of the pools was closed, but a shocking first encounter for a reported five star hotel.
At breakfast we were forgotten by a server on multiple occasions and waited 30 minutes to get our coffee. The hostess also struggled with crowd control and there is often a line for breakfast.
- pools were extremely overcrowded, they shouldn’t be closing one of the pools for an event when majority of guests are not affiliated with the event.
- service at the beach can be very slow and if you miss the waiter it could be an hour until you see them again.
- the rooms are very loud, we had to hook our phones up to the Bluetooth to play white noise.
- this is not a kid friendly hotel, their website even says it’s best for couples and solo travelers. That said, there are hoards of misbehaved children. If you are looking for a romantic, adult focused resort, look else where.

text.text:
My stay at **Andaz Miami Beach** was nothing short of exceptional — a true 5-star property delivering a 5-star experience from start to finish.

I arrived looking for refuge from a snowstorm, and the property manager could not have been more gracious. He kindly upgraded my room, which was such a thoughtful gesture, and even sent a personal note along with a delicious treat waiting for me. That level of care and attention immediately made me feel welcomed and valued.

The room was absolutely beautiful — elegant, comfortable, and immaculately maintained. The pools were stunning and perfectly heated, making it easy to relax and unwind. While there are no hot tubs (which makes sense for Florida’s climate), one would certainly be a nice addition during the cooler winter months. The beach experience was just as lovely, and having two chairs and umbrellas included in the resort fee made it effortless to enjoy the oceanfront setting.

Although I didn’t have the opportunity to dine at the main restaurant, the poolside restaurant was delicious. We tried the burgers, salad, and salmon — all fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared. It was the perfect complement to a relaxing day by the pool.

Another major plus: when paying fully with points, there were no additional fees — a rare and much-appreciated benefit that adds incredible value.

From the warm, personalized service to the beautiful accommodations and amenities, everything exceeded expectations. I would absolutely return — a flawless escape when I needed it most. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

text.text:
My experience with the hotel restaurant was extremely disappointing for a hotel of this category.

On two consecutive days — March 7, 2026 and March 8, 2026 — I arrived about 10–15 minutes before the official closing time of the restaurant (10:30 PM one day and 10:00 PM the next) and was not allowed to be seated by the hostess, who said the kitchen had already closed. However, this information is not communicated to guests anywhere.

In other words, the hotel advertises certain restaurant hours, but in practice the service ends well before that. At the same time, guests who are already seated are not asked to leave at the posted closing time, which makes the situation even more inconsistent.

The attendant suggested ordering through room service, which according to the menu operates from 11 AM to 10 PM. However, when I tried to place the order, I was again told that it would not be possible because the kitchen had already closed.

In other words, even within the posted hours, it is not possible to have dinner either at the restaurant or through room service.

Notably, the same hostess was on duty on both evenings (March 7 and March 8), and the exact same situation occurred both times.

For a hotel in Brickell, this kind of disorganization and lack of transparency regarding restaurant hours, room service availability, and the overall guest experience is quite disappointing.

As someone who frequently stays at Marriott properties, I was surprised by this experience and hope management reviews this policy and ensures that the hours communicated to guests reflect the actual service availability. This experience does not reflect the service standards expected from a Marriott property.

Top notch hotel in the heart of Brickell! Service was immaculate and area was very safe even late at night. Hotel is accessible by the people mover across the street. Tons of shopping and restaurants nearby! Parking is plenty in the attached garage / it is only 30$ for self parking which I’d recommend since valet is 50$ and even if you want to go some place, come back and pay for self parking again, you will still come out on top since it is only 16$ for up to 10 hours!

Room was massive - we had a 1 bed, living, kitchen  and also a washer dryer in room and a large balcony. The room was serviced all days (except for one day and it was quickly resolved with a call to the front desk!) the one complaint about the room is that the tv’s were 20 years old maybe! In this era of digital streaming, these antique ones felt like a time warp!

The bathroom was also dated and the shower nozzles surely need to be cleaned since water went everywhere!

We had complementary breakfast thanks to Amex, it was hearty - the over night oats and French toast are highly recommended!
